messages:
carly wang: Quick heads-up — planning a staggered rolling reboot for the edge GPU pool in us-west1 next Tuesday 03:00-05:00 PST. Objective: apply NIC firmware and kernel micropatchs. Expect ~2h window but we'll do cohorts to keep impact low.

mike henry: Scope? which pools/racks are in the cohort? any tenant exemptions?

carly wang: We'll do 4 cohorts, ~8 racks each. Targeting pool: edge-gpu-01 (NVLink nodes, mostly T4+A10 mix). No tenant exemptions unless explicit enterprise SLA — call out customers we should flag.

sanjay rao: How much capacity do we lose per cohort? I'm worried about queued requests and cold KV cache effects.

carly wang: ~25-30% of edge-gpu capacity per cohort. We plan to warm caches after each cohort and run a 15m canary traffic sweep. We'll keep continuous batching paused for the nodes under drain to avoid long queues.

jen choi: What's the rollback plan if we see high error rates?

leo martinez: Fallback routing configured to send traffic to hosted-general and dedicated-burst for 60m if p95 latency > 800ms or error rate +2%. We also have a model-variant fallback to smaller quantized variants to reduce GPU pressure.

mike henry: Can we surface cost impact? Dedicated burst usage will spike. Need estimate to inform finance.

carly wang: Preliminary: if we move 30% of traffic to dedicated-burst for 2h, estimated incremental spend ~ $3.2k. If we hit hosted-general fallback across regions it's ~ $5k. Will refine after final cohort sizing.

ops-bot: Maintenance ticket created: MAINT-2026-045. Slack notif and incident page will auto-update.

taylor ng: Can infra oncall be on call for the window? I can cover 02:30-06:00 PST.

mike henry: I'll be available for canary validation and quick rollbacks. Sanjay — can you prep the cache-warm scripts? Put them under /ops/runbooks/edge-warmup.sh and attach a shortened command we can run during handoff.

sanjay rao: Yep. Script ready. Quick run: `./edge-warmup.sh --pool edge-gpu-01 --cohort 2 --prefixes 50` — warms top 50 prefixes in parallel.

jen choi: Add a smoke test for model output quality after warmup (prompt set: quality-smoke-20). If regression > 6% fail rate, abort and rollback.

leo martinez: We'll also snapshot routing tables before cohort start: `redis-cli SAVE` and configmap backup. If anything odd, we can revert to prior weights.

carly wang: Communication plan: send tenant notice 48h prior, post reminder 2h prior. On the day: post start msg, cohort handoffs, and final completion msg. Ops page will log all timestamps.

mike henry: Suggest doing cohort 1 and 2 overnight, 3 and 4 early morning to align with APAC low-traffic. That reduces customer impact.

carly wang: Agreed. Cohort schedule attached in ticket. Also adding a short post-mortem template so we capture cache warmup times, rollback triggers, and costs.

taylor ng: One more ask — net team to validate BGP flaps won't coincide with the window. @net-team can you confirm a quiet window?

ops-bot: Net team notified. Response expected within 4 business hours.

sanjay rao: FYI — we saw a similar NIC FW rollout last month; warmup was slower than expected (median 9m vs expected 4m) on older NVLink nodes. I'll add a 10m buffer between cohort start and validation.

jen choi: Noted. I'll update the runbook to record actual warmup durations per cohort.

leo martinez: I'll prepare the quick escalation playbook: steps to re-route at LB layer, how to lift drains, and the cost approval contact for burst spend.

mike henry: LGTM from my side. :thumbsup:

carly wang: Thanks all — I'll push final schedule and tenant comms tomorrow morning. If anyone has objection to the timing, speak up before EOD today.

ops-bot: Maintenance MAINT-2026-045 status: SCHEDULED.
